paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. The people in Joel were staring at ruin, and the LORD didn't leave them there. He heard them, He became jealous for His land, and He spared His people (Joel 2:18). When things look eaten down to the stubs, God is still the One who answers.

Now look at what He promises. He says, "I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts," and He even calls the locusts "My great army that I sent against you" (Joel 2:25). Friend, I lost YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so hearing that God can repay lost years makes my mustache quiver. He doesn't just patch the damage. He fills the threshing floors, He sends the rains, and He says His people will "never again be put to shame" (Joel 2:24, 26).

And why does He do all this? So that His people will know He is present in Israel, and that He is "the LORD your God, and there is no other" (Joel 2:27). The point isn't only the full vats. The point is that you come out of the hard season knowing WHO brought you through it. So if you're sitting in a lean stretch today, baker, take heart: the God who turned weeping into praising for them is the same God you're talking to.
